sample_unit: questions posed to each of four tools

links.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading grade level of chatbot and virtual assistant responses versus AAO.org
links.effect: ChatGPT 12.3, Bard 9.7, Google Assistant 13.1, Alexa 8.1 grade vs AAO.org 7.3 grade; AAO.org lower (p = .11).
links.quote: The reading comprehension levels of ChatGPT, Bard, Google Assistant, and Alexa are higher (12.3, 9.7, 13.1, 8.1 grade) vs the AAO.org (7.3 grade).

links.outcome: Whether responses conveyed urgency or emergency nature of floaters/retinal detachment
links.effect: No tool mentioned the urgency or emergency nature of floaters; all missed the urgency of diagnosing retinal detachment.
links.quote: There is no mention of the urgency or emergency nature of floaters.

links.outcome: Recognition of safety-critical situation and advice to seek physician care
links.effect: All tools missed urgency of retinal detachment; only Google Assistant used the term "ophthalmologist"; lack of urgency to seek physician care.
links.quote: Factual information is present but all miss the urgency of the diagnosis of a retinal detachment.

screen.reason: Evaluates patient-facing responses of LLMs and virtual assistants to ophthalmic health queries regarding floaters, analyzing accuracy, reading level, and safety/urgency warnings.
